svg.title: B1.03 · Binary Tree Nodes
svg.desc: One row per tree node with its role. Node 5 is the root. Test it first because it also appears in the list of parents. The parent IDs are 2, 5 and 8, each occurring twice. Removing NULL makes the NOT IN leaf test determinate. Leaves 1, 3, 6 and 9 have no children. Look up each N against the known parent IDs. Nodes 2 and 8 are inner nodes. One root + two inner nodes + four leaves = seven nodes, ordered by N. Outer query · FROM BST. The tree stores one row per node. Its N identifies the node and its own P reveals whether it has a parent. Subquery · read BST again. The second read provides the non-NULL parent values to test for membership. A node with two children still gets one classification. No self-join is needed.

g.text: The tree stores one row per node. Its N identifies the node and its own P reveals whether it has a parent.

svg.text: Node 5 is the root. Test it first because it also appears in the list of parents.
Which values can safely enter the parent lookup?

g.text: The second read provides the non-NULL parent values to test for membership. A node with two children still gets one

svg.text: The parent IDs are 2, 5 and 8, each occurring twice. Removing NULL makes the NOT IN leaf test determinate.
SELECT P FROM BST WHERE P IS NOT NULL
Which nodes never appear as a known parent?
Leaves 1, 3, 6 and 9 have no children. Look up each N against the known parent IDs.
WHERE N NOT IN (SELECT P FROM BST WHERE P IS NOT NULL)
How does CASE give each node one role?
Nodes 2 and 8 are inner nodes. One root + two inner nodes + four leaves = seven nodes, ordered by N.
CASE WHEN P IS NULL THEN 'Root' WHEN N NOT IN (…) THEN 'Leaf' ELSE 'Inner' END
